actions.fyi: Nothing needed from you. Fog is built, measured, reviewed by someone who did not write it, and on the main line.

content.label: What it looks like
content.lead: The same pit lane at Highlands, same camera, same time of day. Drag the handle.

blocks.text: The cobbles at your feet keep their colour and their grain. The lane dissolves at about the distance you were promised, and the sky and clouds go with it.

shots.caption: Fog, 1 km — the far end of the lane comes back, the hills stay flat
Haze, 10 km — a summer afternoon, distance softened rather than lost

blocks.label: This is the whole point of the fix
blocks.text: Near and far are hit by wildly different amounts, and the amounts line up in order with the weather you asked for. Fog that dimmed everything equally would be a grey filter, not weather.

blocks.label: The hilltops in the dense shot are not a mistake
blocks.text: Fog is a layer with a top. Ground-level fog at 100 m still leaves a hill that rises out of it faintly visible, which is what you see on a real foggy morning from a valley floor.

blocks.label: One thing these pictures do not prove
blocks.text: The whole scene also gets darker in fog, by about two fifths at 100 m. That is the sunlight being absorbed on its way down, and nothing gives that absorbed light back as the soft grey glow real fog has. It is an older approximation, not this work, and I have no measurement saying what the right darkness is.

content.label: It works, and here is the size of it
content.lead: Same yardstick, same six kinds of fog, before and after. Lower is closer to the truth.

rows: Dense fog now reaches the sky instead of leaving it looking clear
The lit haze overhead is roughly right rather than invented
Distance fades at the correct rate at every range
The air between you and the car carries the right amount of light

blocks.label: What is left is not fog
blocks.text: In three of those four measures the worst remaining error is now on the fog-free case — that is the air's own coarseness, with no fog in it at all. Fog itself contributes nothing measurable to the dimming any more.

content.label: How I know it is accuracy and not a different sky
content.lead: The easy way to fake this result is to change the answer and the yardstick together. Two guards stop that.

rows.title: The answer was frozen before a line of fog code moved
rows.note: Twelve reference values captured from the old code. They still hold, untouched, against the new code — so the fog lands where it always landed, it just gets there at real render settings now. Deliberately broken to check it bites: 39 of its 40 comparisons went red, the control stayed green

rows.title: Switching fog off at its one source collapses every case onto clear air, exactly
rows.note: To the last digit, for all five kinds of fog. If anything else in the game were still quietly producing fog, it could not have

blocks.label: And the wider net
blocks.text: 122 tests across sky, cloud, exposure, reflections, shadows and lens. Everything that was green stayed green; the five failures were already failing and already have their own jobs.

content.label: What fog costs

blocks.alt: cost per frame of the stage fog lives in

blocks.text: Milliseconds per frame in the stage that draws the air between you and the car. Dense fog doubles it, and costs a tenth of a millisecond a frame — against a frame budget of about 16.

blocks.label: Read only that one line
blocks.text: The whole-frame figure came out as 1% — near enough to free. It is not a result: work that runs on a rota lands at a different point in its cycle in each of the two runs, so those rows compare schedules, not fog. Filed.

blocks.label: Two things had to be fixed before any number existed
blocks.text: Every performance measurement this project has ever taken was run behind an unthrottled build — the profiler bypassed the limiter that stops this machine freezing. And the comparison tool only ever reported the frame total, never the individual stages, despite our own playbook citing it as the stage-by-stage tool. Fog's cost was invisible to it.

content.lead: Measured six times over, fog on against fog off, same place, alternating so both see the same machine.

content.label: What an outside reader found
content.lead: Someone who did not write it was given the change and told to find the reason it should not land. Verdict: land, with five small fixes. All five are done.

rows.title: A safety check that was only right by luck
rows.note: Two guards a few lines apart were set independently, so a fog roughly three times thicker than the thickest we ship would have slipped between them and produced a wrong picture with no warning. They are now the same check

rows.title: An approximation nobody had written down
rows.note: Looking within a thousandth of a degree of level from above the fog, one shortcut is worth up to a sixth of that sliver's glow. Too narrow to matter, too real to leave unsaid — it is in the debt list now

rows.title: A calculation done every step and read by nobody
Two comments that repeated the design document instead of pointing at it
The same fog-through-the-sun formula has a second hand-written copy elsewhere
rows.note: Older than this work and outside it. Filed as its own job — two copies of one formula is exactly the fault this whole change was undoing

blocks.label: It was also honest about the new guard
blocks.text: The guard added here catches drift; it cannot catch a wrong model, because someone who broke the physics could simply re-record it. That job belongs to the older test that checks the answer against a brute-force one, which this change left alone and which still has teeth.

content.label: Found on the way, now owned

rows.title: A fog fault on the list was already fixed
rows.note: The sky's bounce off the ground ignored fog; earlier work fixed it. That job is dead on arrival

rows.title: The benchmark's own worked example does not work
rows.note: It names a switch that was never built, so that arm silently measures the control against itself and reports no difference

rows.title: The documentation checks grade the wrong copy of the files
rows.note: While work is in progress — which is always — they read the finished copy instead, so they report fixed problems and miss new ones

rows.title: The 250 m rule is not what it was filed as
rows.note: Fog is not hand-drawn near the camera, it is switched off entirely because the grid is too coarse there. This fix removes that reason

rows.title: Two of our own checks are failing on work that is nothing to do with fog
rows.note: One in the tree growing, one in the board's own document. Both were already broken before this landed; both now have owners

decisions.title: Build the exact fog first; re-measure; spread samples only if something is left over
decisions.why: Reverses the plan's stated order, where sample-spreading jumped the queue, and folds a third planned fix in for free. Approved 12 Aug.

decisions.title: The sample-spreading step is paused, not deleted
decisions.why: Its background reading is filed. If the re-measure shows anything left over, it is ready to build immediately.

decisions.title: How the exact fog combines with the air's own dimming over long distances is mine to design
decisions.why: The fog answer is exact for fog alone; the two have to be woven together along the same line of sight. This is the one genuinely unsolved piece.

decisions.title: There is no sunbeam feature — every light interacts with fog and air identically
decisions.why: Ruled 12 Aug and binding on everything downstream: no light may be shadowed in the fog while another is not, and a beam is not a feature, it is what a blocked glow looks like.

decisions.title: The fog's body privilege and the trackside lamps now have owners in the plan
decisions.why: Was written as 'the moon has no shadows'. It has them — the gap is that the fog asks the sun's slot regardless of which body is lighting the scene.

decisions.title: There is no sun and no moon — one kind of body, the same rules for everything
decisions.why: Ruled 12 Aug. Which body it is may be data — its disc, its phase, its colour — never a rule that gives one of them something the other cannot have.

decisions.title: The job is one way in for light, not a fix per kind of light
decisions.why: Ruled 12 Aug. Fog is handed the lights and applies one physics to all of them, so a source built later works by turning up — there is no separate job to add it.

decisions.title: Nothing places a celestial body by hand; the sky obeys the time and the coordinates
decisions.why: Ruled 12 Aug. A body's position is a result of when and where you are, never something you set. The hand-set sun and the switch that reaches it are deleted, so a scene, a test or a preset states a time and a place instead.

decisions.title: D3 is answered: fog is solved exactly over every stretch the render already walks, everywhere, with no exceptions
decisions.why: Dimming from two causes multiplies, so fog and air separate exactly: fog is the thin sharp one and gets solved outright, air is the smooth one and stays sampled. Revised 13 Aug on your call — the first version let the sky and the near air solve fog at different granularities, which would have broken an agreement at the horizon that is currently free. One rule, both paths, no seam to police.

decisions.title: Today's fog is frozen as the thing to be judged against, before anything changes
decisions.why: Otherwise the yardstick moves with the fix and passes whatever happens. This costs a morning and is the difference between a proof and a claim.

decisions.title: The two approximations the design leaves get measured, not argued
decisions.why: Both are small on paper. On paper is not a number, and this project does not ship one.

decisions.title: The sky's remaining glow error is accepted, and it is bounded by the render's coarseness rather than by fog
decisions.why: At its worst it sits beside a fog-free case that is already a fifth as wrong on the same settings, and it shrinks with render quality rather than needing more fog work. Chasing it means turning the sky's step count down, which is its own job with its own number.

decisions.title: The measuring rig got a saved scene with fog on, and the cost is measured
decisions.why: Revised 13 Aug on your correction — I had written this as fog needing a switch built; it does not, the game has had a fog picker all along. What was missing was only a saved scene with fog turned on. Done: dense fog doubles the stage it lives in, for a tenth of a millisecond a frame.

decisions.title: The review's findings were fixed in the same landing, not filed for later
decisions.why: Four of the five are a few lines each and one is a sentence in the debt list. Filing them would have put the weakest version of this work on the main line and left the fixes to argue for themselves later.

decisions.title: The near-level shortcut is written down rather than fixed
decisions.why: It needs a camera above the fog looking within a thousandth of a degree of level. Removing it means giving that one sliver its own maths, which buys a picture nobody will ever frame.

next.if_nothing: Fog is done and on the main line. I say whether it needs any more work from the number we now have, then close the job out.

steps.step: Say whether fog needs more accuracy, from the number rather than the plan
Fog costs nothing at all in clear weather, instead of a little
A saved picture and a horizon check, so this cannot quietly break again
